name: inprocess-obi-apb-two-ip-timer-i2c-multif5-f1f6
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches two independent APB3 MMIO targets by address, and both declare a real IRQ path: the PULP timer's pulse IRQ and the PULP I2C's level IRQ. Every declaring target's real IRQ output is sampled and OR'ed into the CPU's one external interrupt input; one F5 case selects one global link, so its trigger writes, ISR status read, stored cause and clear write all belong to the selected target.
notes: Two APB3 targets both declare complete F5 facts, so this is the multi-declaring-target scenario. Target 0 is the PULP timer at 0x40001000 with configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json: irq_o[0] pulse, trigger writes [[4,0],[8,0],[0,0xffffffff]], status TIMER0_COUNT at offset 0, no clear. Target 1 is the PULP I2C at 0x40002000 with the real interrupt export of configs/peripherals/pulp_i2c_irq/component_profile.json and configs/behaviors/pulp_i2c_level_f5.json: interrupt_o level, trigger writes [[4,0xc0],[16,0x5a],[20,0x10]], status STATUS at offset 0xc with cause bit 0, clear CMD(0x14)=1.

The two behaviors declare the same number of trigger writes (three), which is what one F5 record shape requires: the first record word is one global link index (0 = timer's overflow link, 1 = I2C's level link) followed by that link's three trigger values. A declaration whose links differ in arity is refused by name (unsupported-f5:irq-links-differ-in-arity).

The CPU has one external interrupt input (Ibex machine-external). The host samples every declaring target's real IRQ output per tick and delivers their OR to that one input; per-target counters (target0_irq_high_ticks, target1_irq_high_ticks) and the summary's target<n>_irq delivered state keep the two outputs apart. One F5 case selects one link, so its ISR status read and clear write address that link's own target: simultaneous attribution is not claimed.

Target windows are the profiles' own 4 KiB APB windows: 0x40001000..0x40002000 and 0x40002000..0x40003000, adjacent without overlap. The ZipDMA control window is 0x40003000..0x40003010 and the fixed RAM image is 0x10000..0x30000; no window overlaps another.
The I2C pad inputs scl_pad_i and sda_pad_i are held at 1 (open-drain idle) in both fixed_inputs and tuning.fixed_inputs, as in configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-i2c-level-f5.json.
This file declares the scenario; it is not evidence. The real RTL run under runs/round1-multi-f5/ is the evidence, and it claims only what its case lines read from the devices.
